<note>The text continues a narrative regarding a recluse.</note> Zilu requested to go and call him back. Confucius said: "Let it be. He knows that I have fixed my attention on him. He knows that I am traveling to the State of Chu, and he thinks I will surely cause the King of Chu to summon him. He considers me to be a sycophant. Such a man is ashamed even to hear the words of a sycophant, much less to see his person. Why would he still be there?" Zilu went to look, and the house was empty.

The border warden of Changwu asked Zimu <note>The disciple Zimu</note>, saying: "When you manage the government, do not be reckless. When you govern the people, do not be negligent. In the past <note>The text transitions to a cautionary tale about agricultural neglect as a metaphor for governance</note>

<summary>Confucius advises Zilu against pursuing a recluse who views political involvement as sycophancy. The text then shifts to a border warden advising Zimu on the importance of diligence in governance.</summary>
<keywords>Confucius, Zilu, Zimu, King of Chu, governance, Changwu, recluse, sycophancy, integrity</keywords>
